sections.title: Organic social calendar, October 12 to November 8, 2026
sections.why: Land and lots content earns Mitchell's highest organic engagement but is only 6 percent of posts, so making it the hero on reels, Stories and a first TikTok presence sends warm landowners to the quiz and campaign pages at no media cost.

items.title: How to post this calendar
items.meta: Read first · all channels · posting rules
items.body:
1. Facebook and LinkedIn: paste the caption with that channel's link on the link line. Regional posts already carry both links.
2. Instagram and TikTok: captions say Link in bio. Set the bio link to that post's Instagram or TikTok link the morning it goes up. Instagram allows several bio links, so regional posts can carry both. If the TikTok account cannot show a bio link yet, the end card carries the call to action.
3. YouTube Shorts: links in Shorts captions do not click. Set Related video to the full Behind the Build episode named in the note; its description carries the quiz and Design Dollars links.
4. Stories: use the link sticker with the link listed for that post.
5. The only change between channels is utm_source: facebook, instagram, youtube, tiktok or linkedin.
6. Any piece that mentions Design Dollars keeps the fine print line in the caption and on the image. After October 31, do not repost a Design Dollars caption until Mitchell approves the November reserve by date.
7. Three hashtags at most. No emojis.
items.notes: Default bio link shown here; replace it with each post's link on the day.

items.title: Series idea A: One Question, One Answer
items.meta: Twice a week from October 15 · YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Instagram Reels · 45 to 90 second clips from Behind the Build
items.body:
Format: one question per clip, from an existing Behind the Build episode. The question appears as a text card in the first second, the answer starts right away, captions are burned in, and the end card reads: Answer eight questions. We paint your Home Portrait.

Starter list (question to pull, then episode):
1. Does my land need a well and septic? Well and Septic
2. What should I check before I buy land? Purchasing Land 101
3. What do people get wrong about building on their own land? Common Misconceptions
4. How does the mortgage work when you build? Mortgage 101
5. What is SimplyMitchell? SimplyMitchell Savings
6. What happens after I sign? Contract to Keys
7. What are the steps to build on my land? Homebuyer Roadmap to Success
8. How do I choose fixtures I will still like later? Ferguson Selection Tips

Rules: use the question as the hosts ask it and keep the answer in Mitchell's own words. Cut any build timeline, any savings percentage and any price. On Shorts, set Related video to the full episode, whose description carries the quiz link (Section 3).
items.notes: s03 and s09 are episodes 1 and 2. Give each later clip its own utm_content id (qa03, qa04 and on). Check SimplyMitchell Savings for the old 6.5 percent figure before clipping it.

items.title: Series idea B: Before the House
items.meta: Weekly from October 30 · TikTok first, then Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts · 30 to 60 second land and lot clips
items.body:
Format: a New Home Consultant on a real homesite (owner's permission) answers one land question per clip, in their own words, standing on the ground it is about. TikTok first: the account is empty, and land and lots is the theme that earns Mitchell the most engagement.

Episode prompts:
1. Where does the house go on your land?
2. Where does the driveway go?
3. What is a perc test, and why does it come first?
4. No public water or sewer at the road. Now what?
5. What happens on a land walk?
6. Can my land be my down payment?

Production: film six in one afternoon per division, phone on a gimbal, natural light, warm grade. End card: We build on your land. Link in bio.

Rules: no addresses or neighboring homes in frame, never describe an area as a good place to buy, no prices or savings math, no build timeline.
items.notes: s15 is episode 1. Modeled on the small builder accounts that win on specific land stories. Prompt 6 links /land for Virginia and Southern Maryland.

items.title: Facebook Groups approach
items.meta: Ongoing from October 12 · Facebook Groups (local land, homesteading, rural property, community groups) · Playbook
items.body:
Where: local land for sale, homesteading, rural property and county community groups in each Design Center market. Search the county name with land, acreage or homestead.

Who posts: a named New Home Consultant from their own profile, with Mitchell Homes in their profile. A person reads as a neighbor; a Page reads as an ad.

Rules:
1. Read the group rules first. Business posts only where the rules allow them, or on the admin's promotion day.
2. Value first. Answer the question asked, fully, in the comment, before any mention of Mitchell.
3. Four helpful answers for every one post that mentions Mitchell.
4. No links unless the rules allow them. If allowed, one link, at the end.
5. Always disclose: I work with Mitchell Homes.
6. Never message members who did not ask. Never recommend a county, town or neighborhood or call an area a good place to live (fair housing).
7. No prices, savings figures or the fall offer in groups. Send those questions to a phone call.
8. Log each group, its rules and its promotion day in one sheet.

Time: 20 minutes a day, three days a week, per consultant.
items.notes: Internal playbook. The link is only for groups whose rules allow one.

items.title: Facebook Groups example 1: buying land to build on
items.meta: Any week · Facebook Groups, land and acreage groups · Helpful post
items.body:
Buying land to build a house on? Five things I would check before you commit.

1. Access. Is there legal road frontage or a recorded easement to the parcel?
2. Septic. Has the soil been evaluated for a septic system? If not, ask about a perc or soil test before closing.
3. Water. Is there public water at the road, or will you need a well?
4. Power. How far is the nearest line from where the house would sit?
5. Rules. Zoning, setbacks and any restrictive covenants recorded on the deed.

Your county planning and health departments have the final word on all of these, and a survey settles the boundaries.

I work with Mitchell Homes. We build on land people already own, so these questions come up every week. Happy to answer anything in the comments. Our Behind the Build episode Purchasing Land 101 goes deeper: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=trgJ8maymOA
items.notes: If the group bans links, end at the comments line.

items.title: Facebook Groups example 2: no public water or sewer
items.meta: Any week · Facebook Groups, homesteading and rural property groups · Helpful post
items.body:
No public water or sewer on your land? Here is the order it usually goes when you build.

First, a soil evaluation shows whether and where a septic system can go. That spot shapes where the house can sit.
Next, the well site gets planned at the required distance from the septic area. Your county or state health department sets those distances.
Then the house, the driveway and the power line get placed around both.

It is a normal part of building on rural land, and it is worth doing before you settle on a house spot.

I work with Mitchell Homes, and we build on land people already own. Our Behind the Build episode on well and septic walks through it: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zWwtw8qgp4w
items.notes: Keep it general; state and county rules differ.

items.title: Local partner ideas
items.meta: Start week of October 19 · Each Design Center market · Partner list
items.body:
1. Land surveyors. They meet buyers the moment a parcel becomes real. Offer the Behind the Build land episodes as client education and a direct line to a New Home Consultant.
2. Land listing agents and land auction firms. Agents who list acreage hear what can I build here every week.
3. Farm Credit associations. They finance land purchases and know which members are ready to build.
4. Cooperative Extension offices (Virginia Cooperative Extension, N.C. Cooperative Extension, Clemson Cooperative Extension, University of Maryland Extension). They run landowner and homestead workshops; offer a Homebuyer Roadmap to Success session.
5. Home builders associations. Start with the three associations Mitchell already belongs to and ask for a consumer event slot.
6. Rural electric cooperatives. Ask about member events and newsletters.
7. Well drillers, septic designers and soil scientists. Same parcels, mutual referrals.

Fair housing: partners may share Mitchell's links; Mitchell never recommends where to buy.
items.notes: Confirm the current realtor program terms before offering anything to agents.

items.title: Partner outreach message
items.meta: Start week of October 19 · Email or LinkedIn message from a New Home Consultant · One paragraph
items.body: Hi [Name], I am [Your name], a New Home Consultant at the Mitchell Homes [Studio] Design Center. Mitchell has built custom homes on land people already own since 1992, so many of the people you work with end up asking us the question you probably hear too: what can I build here, and how does the money work? I would like to be a useful resource for your clients, not another sales pitch. We have short Behind the Build episodes on purchasing land and on well and septic that you are welcome to share, and I am glad to meet a client of yours on their land and tell them plainly what it would take to build. Could we have coffee in the next two weeks? [Phone]
items.notes: Send from the consultant, not a generic inbox. Attach the two episode links from FACTS.md.

sections.title: One page summary: every tactic ranked
